brief: UBS's Global Markets Outlook stress-tests four scenarios: oil at $60/bbl, oil at $150/bbl, US Treasury yields at 6.5%, and AI disappointment. The oil scenarios are asymmetric, with cheap oil adding little growth and expensive oil removing far more. The $150/bbl case now does only half the growth damage UBS estimated in March, since the price rise is modelled as spread over 2026-27 rather than within one year. The 6.5% yield scenario kept self-correcting, as central banks responded to the resulting weakness so fast that yields would not hold at 6.5%, forcing UBS to assume inflation stickiness to slow them. AI disappointment is the most damaging scenario. A 25% equity correction cuts household equity wealth by 60% of GDP, on par with the GFC and dot-com bust, removing a large part of US consumption. That hits hyperscalers' revenue and free cash flow, cutting AI capex further. Global growth falls roughly 1pp in 2027 and 2028 versus baseline, 12 economies enter recession, unemployment rises 1.3pp over two years, EUR/USD returns to 1.20, gold reaches $7,000, and several central banks cut to the zero lower bound.
